subject: Renewal paperwork + capacity addendum — sequencing & retention Qs
messages:
From: Hannah Cole <h.cole@arborasystems.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@arborasystems.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal paperwork and Q1 capacity sequencing

Hi Lukas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward with the 18-month renewal and the incremental capacity addendum, but legal asked us to send a single consolidated order form showing the sequencing (Q1 burst to 500k tokens/month, steady-state 300k) and the proposed retention/coverage windows. Attached is our proposed OrderForm with the scheduling notes.

Two quick asks from our side before we route to procurement:
- Confirm whether Redwood can commit to the coverage schedule in Exhibit F during the Q1 burst (we need a fallback if capacity is constrained).
- Clarify the data retention term for logs (we currently have a 24-month requirement; your standard is 12 months).

Can you loop in whoever will own the contractual redlines? Contracts want to see MSA exhibit changes tracked.

Thanks —
Hannah Cole
Sr. Procurement Manager, Arbora Systems
Hannah.Cole@arborasystems.com
Attachment: Arbora_Proposed_OrderForm_v2.docx (Order form with schedule)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cole <h.cole@arborasystems.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork and Q1 capacity sequencing

Hannah —

Appreciate the doc; received the proposed order form. Looping in Naomi (AE) and Marcus (Legal) to own pricing and redlines respectively. Aditya from SRE is cc'd to confirm operational fallback behavior for the Q1 burst.

Preliminary notes:
- We can map the burst/steady-state sequencing in a single Order Form and include a short runbook in Exhibit F for fallback (autoscale to dedicated reserve or temporary model variant fallback). Aditya, can you confirm whether we can commit to the coverage windows in the attached schedule?
- Retention: our standard audit/log retention is 12 months for token-level logs. For customers with compliance needs we can negotiate 24 months with an add-on (we'll need to update Exhibit E and the Data Processing Schedule). Marcus — happy to push a redline for the 24-month option as an addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to send an Exhibit F + Order Form redline that tracks the burst/steady-state language and retention options.
2) Naomi to lock pricing/term and confirm deal milestone dates in HubSpot.
3) Aditya to confirm fallback mechanics and expected RTO for burst overflow.

If that works, Marcus — can you aim for a redline by Friday so Arbora's procurement has something to review next week?

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Strategic Accounts — Renewal Lead, Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-orderform-diff.pdf (diff of sequencing suggestions)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cole <h.cole@arborasystems.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork and Q1 capacity sequencing

Hi Hannah / team —

Thanks — quick pricing clarity: the burst to 500k tokens for Q1 can be accommodated under an annualized uplift with a 20% short-term premium for the first quarter, or we can structure a committed uplift that phases in over the first 90 days to avoid the premium. I recommend the phased-commit approach since it keeps unit economics predictable.

I've updated the HubSpot deal (link below) with the two options and the ACV impact. If Arbora is comfortable with the phased commitment, we'll prepare the Order Form with the phased quantities and a clause that the initial burst is subject to our temporary model-fallback policy (no penalty if fallback used).

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ARB-2026-023

Proposed next step on my end: confirm pricing option by Thursday EOD so we can finalize paperwork ahead of procurement review next week.

Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cole <h.cole@arborasystems.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 14:56:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork and Q1 capacity sequencing — redlines attached

Hannah / Lukas —

Attached is a tracked redline of Exhibit F and the Order Form showing the sequencing language and two retention options (12 months standard; 24 months elective addendum). High-level summary of legal changes:

1) Exhibit F (Coverage & Sequencing): added Section 2.3 to define burst window, fallback priority (Dedicated Reserve > Model Variant > Regional Overflow), and a requirement for 72-hour notice for scheduled large-scale bursts.

2) Data retention / logs: added a Data Processing Schedule addendum that permits a 24-month retention option by separate fee schedule; otherwise the default remains 12 months.

3) Liability / SLA: clarified that fallback to model-variant or regional overflow preserves service but may change latency SLAs; added explicit language that capacity fallback is not a breach so long as Redwood makes commercially reasonable efforts to provide the committed quantities.

Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachment: MSA-exhibit-F-proposed-redline.docx (tracked changes)

Thanks everyone — helpful summary, appreciate the speed. Procurement has two narrow asks before they can sign:

1) Can we get explicit language that the temporary fallback will not block Arbora from using a pre-approved alternate provider for urgent bursts if Redwood cannot supply capacity within 48 hours? (Tom — this is their legal point.)
2) For the optional 24-month retention, can you provide a one-line fee schedule estimate so procurement can budget?

If you can add those two items to the redline and share an editable version (we prefer tracked changes in Word), procurement will push this through next week. Also please send a DocuSign starter link once redlines are mutually finalized.

Hannah Cole
Sr. Procurement Manager, Arbora Systems
